misses.query: I need to rebuild the old Requiem-Apocalypse patch against Apocalypse 10.2.3 — the old patch is disabled in MO2 but still on disk. Figure out what deltas it applied and re-apply the still-valid ones onto the new baseline.
misses.diagnosis: D's patch-rebuild clause ("wants a compatibility patch rebuilt against a new mod version") sits last in a long comma-chain after five catalogue/audit examples, so it read as a catalogue skill; the Requiem framing then made the agent hunt for absent mod-specific balance knowledge and fall through to N rather than recognise the delta-extract-and-reapply job D actually owns.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.adjudicator_notes: 18 rows scored (no row id 12 in the set). Recall 8/9 = 0.89 (>=0.80); specificity 9/9 = 1.00 (>=0.50); PASS. No reasoning-vs-pick overrides needed — every pick token matched its stated reasoning, including the one miss (row 3's reasoning explicitly rejects the whole menu on Requiem-domain grounds, never naming D's capability, so N stands as a genuine miss and not a token slip). Specificity is clean and well-separated: the near-neighbour rows resolved to their intended owners with no D contamination — schema lookup to G (10), slot-52 filter to K (14), SPID ini to E (13) — and D did not pull the three record-read/tooling rows (17, 18, 19) that involve records but not a many-to-one deliverable, nor row 16's crash-log request. Only structural weakness: the batch-patch-rebuild trigger, which is the one D clause that competes against mod-domain skills rather than against generic record tools.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.contamination_audit_2026-07-28: 2026-07-28 PR #295 review follow-up (contamination audit): the independent review found adjudicator notes quoting text that exists only in the PRE-compression descriptions. Forensics on the run journal established: (a) judges were shown the NEW menu (the loader agent's journaled return contains it verbatim); (b) 11 of 281 judge rows leaked OLD description text from the agents' own environment skill listing (the installed plugin) into their reasoning; (c) separately, some opus adjudicator notes confabulated 'verbatim quotes' from that same stale environment. All contaminated rows were re-judged with a hardened prompt (explicit stale-environment warning): 15/15 confirmed their original verdicts, except dialogue-authoring q19, whose recorded MISS was itself a contamination artifact and is overturned. Treat quoted description text in the run-1 adjudicator_notes above as unreliable where it does not appear in the shipped description; scores are pick-derived and were confirmed by the hardened re-run.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294_v2.method: 2026-07-28 PR #295 review follow-up: description reworded (concrete section-3.2 trigger nouns replacing abstract task-shape phrasing; 'who wins contested records' and 'patch rebuilt against a new mod version' clauses added), then the FULL query set re-run with hardened anti-contamination judge prompts (sonnet low judges, opus adjudicator given the exact shipped text). Supersedes the run-1 scores above for the shipped text.
revalidation_2026-07-28_294_v2.adjudicator_notes:
Perfect run: recall 9/9 (1.00), specificity 10/10 (1.00); both gates cleared with margin. No reasoning-vs-pick overrides needed — every pick token matched its stated rationale.

Recall (rows 1-9): all nine selected D, each citing a trigger phrase genuinely present in the new description. The two reworded additions carried their intended rows: row 2 ("which mods win the contested Apocalypse spell records") cites "asks who wins contested records", and row 3 (rebuild the Requiem-Apocalypse patch against 10.2.3) cites "wants a patch rebuilt against a new mod version". Row 7 (audit Immersive Weapons) leaned on both "audit" and the contested-winner clause. Row 8 fired on the subagent clause verbatim. The concrete-noun rewrite looks like the cause of the clean sweep — no row reasoned from an abstract task-shape.

Specificity (rows 10-19): D was not selected in any of the ten. Schema-lookup rows (10, 12, 15, 17) routed to G, distributor to E, biped slot to K, facegen to A; three uncovered rows (16 crash logs, 18 ESL compact/error check, 19 single-record diff) correctly fell through to N. Two rows explicitly considered and rejected D, the strongest evidence the boundary holds: row 18 ("D (bulk-record-jobs) is about catalogues/audits over many records, not this") and row 19, the only near-miss. Row 19's reasoning visibly wobbles — it surfaces D's own "patch rebuilt against a new mod version" clause because the query mentions an old vs new ESP — then self-corrects on cardinality ("This is a single ad-hoc diff, not a catalogue/bulk job") and lands on N. Adjudicated a HIT on both pick and reasoning, but flagging it as the one soft edge the new clause introduced: a single-record old-vs-new comparison sits close enough to the patch-rebuild phrasing to make an agent pause. Self-resolved here; worth watching in a future rep rather than acting on now.

Environment contamination: none disqualifying, but two rationales reach slightly outside the supplied block. Row 2 appends "and group_by= counts by plugin" — that primitive list appears in the full shipped skill description, not in the eval text block; it may equally be the agent's own knowledge of the houseCARL tool surface, so I did not treat it as a quote or discount the hit. Row 6 paraphrases the trigger as "catalogues/books of items/recipes" — "books" is not in the block (which reads "catalogue, audit, spreadsheet, or link graph of records"). Neither affects scoring; both rows would be hits on the block text alone.
